verdict.rationale: Paxos documents first-party webhooks. Users register their own endpoints in the Dashboard, choose event types, and secure delivery with API Key or OAuth auth and a configurable RPS limit. The docs also cover 24-hour retries, a List Events API for recovering failed deliveries, test events, and orchestration event families. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration, and evidence that webhooks can be registered programmatically through an API rather than only via the Dashboard.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks

citations.quote: Paxos Webhooks allow you to register your own endpoints to receive asynchronous events driven by the Paxos Platform.
Configure your webhook with the relevant name, endpoint, event types, auth type (API Key or OAuth), auth config, and RPS.
Paxos will continue retry attempts for up to **24 hours** from the initial attempt, unless delivery succeeds.
Use the [List Events](/api-reference/endpoints/events/list-events) API to query for events that may have failed delivery
Use the Test feature in Dashboard to send a test event to your webhook
